It contains the only industrial use, a lithograph company, located on the extreme eastern side. It also contains the Virginia Home (for incurables) facing Byrd Park on the extreme western edge. Four schools are located within the area and each has adjacent recreation space. This area is largely single family detached homes, although there area many multi-family structures generally located along the northern edge. For most of its common border with Area One a distinct encroachment of blight and blighting influence is obvious. Several blocks, generally between Lakeview Avenue and Winder Street, and Allen Street and Randolph Street (see map), have considerable blight, decay, and neglect as found in Area One. These areas are generally beyond rehabilitation. In total the blighted sections although significant and growing in size, constitute approximately one fifth of the land area with Area Three. Area Three shares physical characteristics of both Areas One and Two. Although single family detached homes are in the majority, row-type and multiple family structures also exist. Although the largest land area of the three areas, it has the smallest density. Most structures are of modest construction, many are well maintained and exhibit a pride of ownership. Streets are narrow and most have parking problems, but not the through traffic problems associated with the other areas. Open space is more abundant within this area than the other two. It is also bordered on almost three sides by open areas. The Maymont Community adjacent to the southwestern edge of Area Three does not exhibit blighting influences and was described in more detail in other areas of this report. Area Three has redevelopment and rehabilitation. It could become a sound residential environment or it could become another Area One.
b. Environment Deficiencies of Existing Conditions
To sum up the current physical character of a large portion of the Randolph Area is deficient in the following respects:
(1) Overcrowding or improper location of buildings on the land. A number of residential lots are 15-20 feet wide and house one or two families. No parking or open space is available to these residents.
